Declarations and API

The main theorems and the principal intermediate results are the starting points for readers using the library.

Declaration under ExtriangulatedRealizationPurpose
theoremATheorem A (Theorem 4.5): an essentially small k-linear extriangulated category with no triangulated embedding, with countable local algebraic realizations
theoremBTheorem B (Theorem 3.1): C(D) has a triangulated embedding iff every projection lim D → D_i is surjective iff it has an algebraic realization
theoremB_necessityTheorem 3.1, (1) ⇒ (2): a triangulated embedding into a category in any universe forces the projections to be surjective
proposition_2_3Proposition 2.3: compatible surjections from one vector space make C_J extriangulated with an algebraic realization
corollary_2_4Corollary 2.4: C(D) is an essentially small extriangulated category; each C_J is extension-closed and extriangulated, and realized when J has a largest element
proposition_4_4Proposition 4.4: idempotent complete, Krull–Schmidt, indecomposables X, Y, A_i, P_i with endomorphism ring k, table (4.1), enough injectives, E² = 0
proposition_4_6Proposition 4.6: a countable cofinal subset or finite-dimensional D_i give an algebraic realization
Injections.example_4_2Example 4.2: injections of countable ordinals into ℕ give a category with no triangulated embedding
isAlgebraicTriangulated_homotopyCategoryThe homotopy category of an additive category is algebraic triangulated
cd_exists_realizesEvery extension of C(D) is realized (Construction 2.2, Lemma 2.1)
isIdempotentComplete_CDC(D) is idempotent complete, by splitting triangular idempotents
rank_ext_singleTable (4.1): the dimensions of E between indecomposables
linearize_compatible_eq_zeroLemma 4.1: lim k^(S_i) = 0 when lim S = ∅ and countable index sets are bounded
